title: What arrived first: the running comparisons
happened: The day before, the video game GTA VI had been released, and for years people had joked about what would happen before it came out. Several accounts noted that the hypothesis had almost come first: one said 'almost', a small member insisted it had not, and chordbug read a line in the note about 'horrible timing' as regret at missing that joke by a day. A second comparison came from screenshots of a mathematician's old posts mocking the idea that AI would prove the hypothesis in 2026 before Apple shipped an LLM-powered Siri, with his gracious concession that day; norvid said he too was surprised the Riemann tech came first, and replies offered their own list of things still waiting (self-driving cars, faster-than-light travel, a purely visual Pokémon run), until a member pointed out that Siri already runs on Gemini and norvid admitted he could not fact-check that. A third was the Millennium Prize scoreboard: a joke that all the problems might be solved with none of the prize money claimed, whether the prize even covers the token cost, and a prediction that P vs NP will be last. foremphasis quoted his own earlier guess of a headline about the hypothesis being solved in 2.5 million lines of Lean 'to little fanfare' with 'might have undershot just a bit'. joetforhire posted a screenshot of a July post predicting the hypothesis would fall on 21 November 2026, and members admired the date. And yetanotheruseless said he was less worried about Claude solving RH than about a bot with 3 brain cells becoming Top Chicken before him. The show can assert nothing about whether the proof (or the human proof mentioned here) is correct; on 20 November it was a claim being checked, and these posts are people reacting to the claim.

couldBeShown: The comparisons are a list the community wrote itself: GTA VI (released the day before), LLM-powered Siri, self-driving cars, faster-than-light travel, a purely visual Pokémon run, Top Chicken, P vs NP, the Millennium Prize money. chordbug's image (alt): 'The precise timing is horrible.' and the following lines of the note. mergesort's three screenshots (alt): Daniel Litt, 9/29/25, 'guy who thinks he'll win a millenium prize for typing "prove the Riemann Hypothesis. don't make any mistakes."'; 3/8/25, 'person who thinks AI will prove the Riemann hypothesis in 2026 but that Apple won't deliver an LLM-powered Siri'; 11/20/26, 'Seems like I was wrong about this!'. joetforhire's image (no alt, fetched): a screenshot of an X post by 'Myk is Walking Backwards' (@mykola), 9:16 PM, Jul 20, 2026, 71.3K views: 'It's November 21st, 2026. The Riemann hypothesis falls ... and the proof fits in a tweet', followed by invented future dates (P = NP on January 22, 2027, Gödel falling on February 9, 'The Song' first played February 14). mrcheeze's image: a Wikipedia section on barriers to proving P vs NP.
